group.passage: Mount Wellington rises above Hobart, the capital of the Australian state of Tasmania, and more than 400,000 people visit it each year, most of them driving up a single winding road. A cable car to the top was first suggested in 1905. The latest plan, a $54 million line with three towers, was turned down by the city council in 2021, and the company’s appeal failed at a planning tribunal in 2022, which found problems with its noise, its visual impact, and its effects on the mountain’s rocks and wildlife. In 2024, however, the state government began reviewing how the mountain should be managed, and the idea came back. Of more than 9,000 public comments sent to the review, 30 percent backed a cable car and 28 percent opposed one.

passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: Text A: A hotel owner’s letter
passage_parts.text: I run a small hotel in Hobart, and every winter I watch guests miss the chance to see our mountain. Snow and ice often close the road in the colder months, and visitors who have flown halfway around the world go home without the view. On those days the only way up is a long, steep walk that older people and wheelchair users cannot manage. A cable car would run in almost any weather. Meanwhile, visitor numbers are expected to double within 25 years. Would we rather carry those people quietly through the air, or let thousands more cars crawl up the road? Every tourist who stays an extra day means work for local cooks, guides, and drivers. Our mountain deserves better than a crowded car park.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: Text B: A plant scientist’s column
passage_parts.text: I have studied the plants of Mount Wellington for twenty years, and I worry less about the view than about what lies beneath it. The line that was rejected in 2021 would have passed in front of the Organ Pipes, columns of rock up to 120 meters tall that formed when dinosaurs still walked the earth. A new building at the summit would also have damaged alpine plants that have taken centuries to develop. Of course, the mountain is already under pressure, and doing nothing is not an answer. But a cable car would invite more visitors. A better plan is to manage the crowds we already have, for example by charging cars a fee and spending the money on trails and repairs. A recent report estimated that such a fee could cut visitor numbers by 29 percent. The aim should be to protect the mountain, not to sell it.

questions.stem: On which of the following would both writers most likely agree?

options.A: A cable car would reduce the traffic on the mountain road.
options.B: The number of people visiting the mountain should be reduced.
options.C: The mountain already faces problems that call for action.
options.D: The council was right to turn down the plan in 2021.

questions.stem: What does the writer of Text A mean by saying that the mountain “deserves better than a crowded car park”?

options.A: The mountain should not be overrun by cars.
options.B: The car park at the summit should be made larger.
options.C: Hotels should offer more parking spaces for their guests.
options.D: Visitors should pay more to park on the mountain.

questions.stem: Which of the following is presented as a fact rather than an opinion?

options.A: A cable car would bring more work to local cooks, guides, and drivers.
options.B: Charging cars a fee is a better plan than building a cable car.
options.C: A cable car would draw still more visitors to the mountain.
options.D: The route turned down in 2021 was planned to go past some very tall rock formations.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true according to the texts?

options.A: The plan turned down in 2021 was the first cable car idea for the mountain.
options.B: The tribunal did not overturn the council’s decision on the plan.
options.C: Most people who sent comments to the review wanted a cable car.
options.D: The road to the summit is closed for most of the year.

1.explanation_zh: A 說訪客人數預計會加倍，不想讓更多車子擠上山路，並說這座山「值得比擁擠的停車場更好的待遇」；B 也說這座山已經承受壓力，「什麼都不做不是辦法」。兩人開出的方法不同（A 要纜車、B 要收費管理人潮），但都認為現況有問題、必須採取行動，所以選 C。
evidence: Would we rather carry those people quietly through the air, or let thousands more cars crawl up the road?
Our mountain deserves better than a crowded car park.
Of course, the mountain is already under pressure, and doing nothing is not an answer.

option_notes_zh.A: 只有 A 的看法：A 認為纜車能取代開車上山；B 則認為纜車只會招來更多訪客。
option_notes_zh.B: 只有 B 的看法：B 主張用收費減少訪客；A 是飯店業者，希望遊客多停留，並沒有要減少人數。
option_notes_zh.D: B 反對纜車，可能同意駁回；但 A 支持興建纜車，不太可能認為駁回是對的。

A: Would we rather carry those people quietly through the air, or let thousands more cars crawl up the road?
But a cable car would invite more visitors.
B: A better plan is to manage the crowds we already have, for example by charging cars a fee and spending the money on trails and repairs.
Every tourist who stays an extra day means work for local cooks, guides, and drivers.
D: A cable car would run in almost any weather.
The line that was rejected in 2021 would have passed in front of the Organ Pipes, columns of rock up to 120 meters tall that formed when dinosaurs still walked the earth.

1.strategy_zh: 多文本「兩人都同意」的題目，要把每個選項分別拿去對 A 和 B：只符合其中一人的立場，就是陷阱。立場相反的兩篇文章，共識常在「問題存在」，分歧在「怎麼解決」。
hints: A 對山上現況有什麼不滿？
B 說這座山現在處於什麼狀態？
A 和 B 對「要不要減少遊客」看法一樣嗎？

2.explanation_zh: A 前一句問：我們寧願讓遊客安靜地從空中上山，還是讓成千上萬輛車在路上緩慢爬行？接著說這座山「值得比擁擠的停車場更好的待遇」。意思是不該讓這座山被大量汽車佔據、變成擁擠的停車場，所以選 A。
evidence: Would we rather carry those people quietly through the air, or let thousands more cars crawl up the road?
Our mountain deserves better than a crowded car park.

option_notes_zh.B: 字面義：作者不是要把停車場擴大，反而是不希望山上擠滿車子。
option_notes_zh.C: 上下文看似可通：寫信者經營旅館，但這句話談的是山上的車潮，不是旅館的停車位。
option_notes_zh.D: 細節錯置：向汽車收費是 B 提出的辦法，不是 A 這句話的意思。

D: A better plan is to manage the crowds we already have, for example by charging cars a fee and spending the money on trails and repairs.

2.strategy_zh: 比喻或強調句要回到上下文：前一句把「空中纜車」和「更多車子爬上山路」對比，就知道「擁擠的停車場」是指車滿為患的情況。
hints: 前一句拿哪兩種上山方式比較？
「擁擠的停車場」代表的是好的還是不好的情況？

3.explanation_zh: B 說 2021 年被駁回的路線原本會從管風琴岩（Organ Pipes）正前方經過；這是關於路線位置、可以查證的事實。其他三個選項都是作者的預測或主張（would、better），屬於意見，所以選 D。
evidence: The line that was rejected in 2021 would have passed in front of the Organ Pipes, columns of rock up to 120 meters tall that formed when dinosaurs still walked the earth.

option_notes_zh.A: 這是 A 的預測（would），用來支持興建纜車，無法當成已經發生的事實。
option_notes_zh.B: 這是 B 的主張（A better plan），屬於意見。
option_notes_zh.C: 這是 B 的推測（would），屬於意見。

A: Every tourist who stays an extra day means work for local cooks, guides, and drivers.
B: A better plan is to manage the crowds we already have, for example by charging cars a fee and spending the money on trails and repairs.
C: But a cable car would invite more visitors.

3.strategy_zh: 事實與意見題：看到 would、should、better、best 這類預測或評價字眼，多半是意見；能查證的地點、時間、數字才是事實。
hints: 哪些選項用了 would 或 better？
哪個選項描述的是可以查證的路線位置？

4.explanation_zh: 引言說這個計畫 2021 年被市議會否決，公司向規劃仲裁機構提出的上訴在 2022 年也失敗了。上訴失敗代表仲裁機構沒有推翻市議會的決定，所以選 B。
evidence: The latest plan, a $54 million line with three towers, was turned down by the city council in 2021, and the company’s appeal failed at a planning tribunal in 2022, which found problems with its noise, its visual impact, and its effects on the mountain’s rocks and wildlife.

option_notes_zh.A: 與原文相反：早在 1905 年就有人提議蓋纜車。
option_notes_zh.C: 數字陷阱：支持纜車的意見占 30%，反對的占 28%，支持的人雖然比反對的多，但遠不到「大多數」。
option_notes_zh.D: 過度概括：A 說的是在較冷的月份常因冰雪封路，不是一年中大部分時間都封閉。

A: A cable car to the top was first suggested in 1905.
C: Of more than 9,000 public comments sent to the review, 30 percent backed a cable car and 28 percent opposed one.
D: Snow and ice often close the road in the colder months, and visitors who have flown halfway around the world go home without the view.

4.strategy_zh: 細節題要注意比例與範圍：30% 比 28% 多，不代表「大多數」；「冬天常封路」不等於「一年大部分時間封路」。「上訴失敗」要轉換成「原決定被維持」。
hints: 公司的上訴結果如何？這對市議會的決定有什麼影響？
纜車的構想最早是哪一年提出的？
支持纜車的意見占多少百分比？算得上大多數嗎？

translation_zh.text:
威靈頓山聳立在澳洲塔斯馬尼亞州的首府荷巴特上方，每年有超過 400,000 人造訪，其中大多數人開車沿著唯一一條蜿蜒的道路上山。早在 1905 年就有人提議蓋一條通往山頂的纜車。最近一次的計畫是一條造價 5,400 萬（澳幣）、有三座塔架的纜車線，2021 年被市議會否決；公司的上訴也在 2022 年被規劃仲裁機構駁回，仲裁機構認為它在噪音、視覺衝擊，以及對山上岩石與野生動植物的影響上都有問題。然而在 2024 年，州政府開始檢討這座山該如何管理，蓋纜車的構想又回來了。在送交這次檢討的 9,000 多則民眾意見中，30% 支持蓋纜車，28% 反對。
【A：一位旅館業者的投書】我在荷巴特經營一家小旅館，每年冬天都看著房客錯失欣賞這座山的機會。在較冷的月份，冰雪常常讓道路封閉，飛越半個地球而來的遊客只能看不到美景就回家。那些日子裡，上山唯一的方法是走一段又長又陡的路，年長者和坐輪椅的人根本走不了。纜車幾乎在任何天氣都能運行。與此同時，訪客人數預計在 25 年內加倍。我們是寧願讓這些人安靜地從空中上山，還是讓成千上萬輛車在路上緩慢爬行？每一位多住一天的遊客，都代表本地廚師、導遊和司機多了一份工作。我們的山值得比擁擠的停車場更好的待遇。
【B：一位植物學者的專欄】我研究威靈頓山的植物已經二十年，比起景觀，我更擔心景觀底下的東西。2021 年被駁回的那條路線，原本會從管風琴岩前方經過；那是一根根高達 120 公尺的岩柱，形成於恐龍還在地球上活動的年代。在山頂蓋新建築，也會破壞花了好幾百年才長成的高山植物。當然，這座山已經承受壓力，什麼都不做不是辦法。但纜車只會招來更多訪客。比較好的做法是管理現有的人潮，例如向汽車收費，再把錢用在步道和維修上。最近一份報告估計，這樣的收費可以讓訪客人數減少 29%。我們的目標應該是保護這座山，而不是把它賣掉。

open_tasks.prompt: Fill in a two-column table comparing the two writers: for each writer, give (1) their position on the cable car and (2) one reason they give. Then write one English sentence saying which argument you find stronger and why.
reference_answers: Text A supports the cable car because it would work in almost any weather; Text B opposes it because it would harm the Organ Pipes and alpine plants. I find Text B stronger because it offers another way to deal with the crowds.

Text A wants the cable car so that older people and wheelchair users can reach the top; Text B prefers charging cars a fee to manage visitors. I find Text A stronger because it thinks about people who cannot walk up.
checklist_zh: 表格是否正確寫出兩人的立場
每人至少一個來自原文的理由
最後一句是否清楚表態並說明理由
